description: Issue #839 AC1, in the HERITAGE `to` spelling of the declaration slot. `spec/grammar.md` gives the grammar four declaration slots and `to` is one of them; `spec/conformance.md:150` makes Heritage "alternate spellings only. It does not add new semantics", so `to foo` twice must be exactly as illegal as `define foo` twice — same code, same params, same spans, differing only where the shorter keyword moves the column (the name starts at column 4 rather than 8). The corpus is the stack-neutral artifact another implementation must satisfy, so a `to`-slot rule pinned only in `packages/runtime` would not be portable. The two bodies print different values so the fixture discriminates between last-wins, first-wins and the ruling's rule. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
